content.text: : Sx inflam of the nasal cavity & paranasal sinuses lasting <4wks
: inflam condition involving paranasal sinuses & nasal passage linings lasting ≥12wks
: IC * pt; Aspergillus spp., Fusarium spp., Mucorales
▪︎sinuses lined by ciliated epithelia + mucus-producing goblet cells; infected → copious mucus conducive to microbial growth
▪︎impaired mucociliary clearance 2/2 nasal mucosal inflam w/ obstruction of the ostiomeatal complexes → mucus accumulation → 2° bacterial infect
▪︎classification: acute <4wk, subacute 4–12wk, chronic >12wk, recurrent acute ≥4 episodes/yr w/ interim sx resolution
Co-Factors: air pollution, nasal polyps, preg, oral HTN, anti-OP, mucocilliary dysfun, rhinitis medicamentosa (rebound congestion)
▪︎complications: orbital cellulitis (frontal/ethmoid), subdural abscess & meningitis (frontal/ethmoid), cavernous sinus thrombosis (sphenoid), frontal bone osteomyelitis (Pott puffy tumor)

▪︎saline irrigation, ibuprofen/APAP, oral decongestants, IN glucocorticoids, mucolytics, topical nasal vasocontrictors
▪︎1st-line: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg-125 mg BID or 500 mg-125 mg TID
▪︎doxycycline 100 mg BID or 200 mg daily; also for hepatic impairment
▪︎IDSA: doxycycline as a general alternative to amox-clav for any adult (⍉only PCN-allergic pts)
▪︎mild-mod Sx → symptomatic tx (NSAIDs, oral + topical decongestants, nasal washing, nasal steroids); ABX reserved for complicated or protracted cases (most resolve w/in 2 wks w/o ABX)
▪︎complicated pts (eg immunocompromised) also benefit from ABX
: amphotericin B ± surg debridement of necrotic tissue
▪︎invasive fungal sinusitis → surgical debridement + systemic voriconazole or lipid formulation amphotericin B
